items.title: Add a `composer sbom` command for CycloneDX and SPDX output
items.body:
<!-- Please remember to select the appropriate branch:

For bug fixes pick the oldest branch where the fix applies (e.g. `2.4` if that version is affected, `1.10` if it is a critical fix that should be fixed in Composer 1, otherwise `main`)

For new features and everything else, use the main branch. -->

Target branch: `main` (new feature).

## Summary

This PR adds a `composer sbom` command. It outputs a Software Bill of Materials for the project's dependencies as CycloneDX 1.6 JSON (the default) or SPDX 2.3 JSON. It reads either the installed packages or, with `--locked`, `composer.lock`. For each package it records the exact version, a `pkg:composer` purl, licenses, source and dist references, the dist SHA-1 when there is one, and the dependency graph. Dev-only packages are marked as such.

## Motivation

More and more projects are being asked for SBOMs. The EU Cyber Resilience Act and US federal software procurement both expect one in a standard format. For PHP projects, Composer already holds all the data an SBOM needs: resolved versions, VCS references, dist URLs and checksums, declared licenses and the require graph. Right now the only way to get that data out in a standard format is a third-party plugin, and each plugin reads the lock file and maps fields its own way.

Composer itself has nothing for this today:

- A search for CycloneDX, purl (`pkg:composer`) or SBOM under `src/` finds nothing apart from this change. The SPDX code that exists is for license validation and display (`composer/spdx-licenses`, used for example by `ShowCommand`), not for writing SBOMs.
- `LicensesCommand` (`src/Composer/Command/LicensesCommand.php:40`) is the closest existing command, and it only supports `text`, `json` and `summary`. None of those carry versions as purls, source/dist references, checksums or dependency edges.
- Recent work on `audit`, and the policy/filter-list changes in the 2.10/2.11 changelog, show that supply-chain tooling is already a focus of the project. SBOM export fits with that work.

The people who benefit most are teams that have to hand an SBOM to customers or auditors for a PHP application. A built-in format would also give Packagist and Private Packagist one canonical output to build on.

## What changed

- **`src/Composer/Command/SbomCommand.php`** (new): The command itself.
  - Options: `--format/-f` (`cyclonedx` | `spdx`, default `cyclonedx`), `--no-dev` and `--locked`.
  - Dispatches the usual `PluginEvents::COMMAND` event so plugins can hook in the same way they do for other commands.
  - Picks the package set the same way `licenses` does: the local repository by default, or `Locker::getLockedRepository(!$noDev)` with `--locked`. In non-locked mode, `--no-dev` filters with `RepositoryUtils::filterRequiredPackages`.
  - Contains the CycloneDX builder, the SPDX builder and shared helpers for purls, licenses and link resolution.
- **`src/Composer/Console/Application.php`**: Registers the command next to `LicensesCommand`.
- **`doc/03-cli.md`**: New `sbom` section with a usage example and the option list, placed right after `licenses`.
- **`tests/Composer/Test/Command/SbomCommandTest.php`** (new): Functional tests through the application tester for both formats and all options (details below).

## How it works

**Package set.** Alias packages are dropped so that each real package shows up once, under its real version. Packages are sorted alphabetically so the order of components is stable between runs. I build a name-to-package map from each package's `getName()`, then fill in the names from `getNames()` (`provide`/`replace`) where no real package already has that name. This means a requirement such as `psr/log-implementation` resolves to the package that provides it. Platform requirements (`php`, `ext-*`) and any other link target with no installed package are left out of the graph.

**Identifiers.** Every package gets a purl of the form `pkg:composer/<vendor>/<name>@<prettyVersion>`, with each segment passed through `rawurlencode`, so `1.0.0+build` becomes `1.0.0%2Bbuild`. In CycloneDX the purl is also used as the `bom-ref`, which keeps references readable and unique for each package/version pair.

**CycloneDX 1.6.**
- The root package goes in `metadata.component` with type `application`. Every dependency becomes a `library` component, and the vendor and name are split into `group` and `name`.
- `scope` is `optional` for packages in the repository's dev package names (`getDevPackageNames()` from the lock or `installed.json`) and `required` for everything else. This uses the dev/non-dev split Composer already computes, which includes transitive dev-only packages, so I did not re-derive it from the graph.
- Licenses: when there is more than one license, they are combined into an SPDX expression `(A OR B)`, because Composer treats multiple licenses as alternatives. That expression is used if it validates. Otherwise each license is listed on its own, as `license.id` when it is a known SPDX identifier and as `license.name` when it is not (custom or proprietary strings).
- `externalReferences` has a `vcs` entry for the source URL and a `distribution` entry for the dist URL. The source or dist reference goes in `comment`, and the dist SHA-1 goes in `hashes` when it is set.
- `dependencies` has one entry for the root, built from `require` plus `require-dev` (unless `--no-dev`), and one entry for each package, built from its `require`.

**SPDX 2.3.**
- Each package becomes an SPDX package with `filesAnalyzed: false`. `licenseConcluded` and `copyrightText` are set to `NOASSERTION`, because Composer has no basis for asserting either.
- `licenseDeclared` is the validated SPDX expression, or `NOASSERTION` when the declared license is not valid SPDX.
- `downloadLocation` is the dist URL when it is an absolute URL. Failing that, it is `<vcs>+<url>@<ref>` for git/hg/svn sources, following the SPDX VCS location syntax. Failing both, it is `NOASSERTION`.
- Relationships: the document `DESCRIBES` the root, runtime requires are `DEPENDS_ON`, and root dev requires are recorded as `<dev package> DEV_DEPENDENCY_OF <root>`.
- SPDX IDs come from the package name with `/` and `_` replaced by `-`. If two names map to the same ID (for example `foo/bar-baz` and `foo/bar_baz`), a numeric suffix is added so the IDs stay unique.
- Each package also carries its purl as a `PACKAGE-MANAGER` external ref, so the SPDX and CycloneDX output can be cross-referenced.

**Credentials.** Every source and dist URL goes through `Url::sanitize()` before it is written. This matters because dist URLs can contain basic-auth credentials or tokens for private repositories, and an SBOM is a document that gets handed to third parties.

**Document identity.** The CycloneDX `serialNumber` and the SPDX `documentNamespace` use a random v4 UUID created with `random_bytes`. Timestamps are UTC in ISO 8601 format. Composer's own version is recorded as the generating tool.

**Alternatives I considered:**
- *Adding `--format=cyclonedx|spdx` to `licenses`.* An SBOM covers much more than licenses: versions, hashes, references and the graph. Putting this in `licenses` would also make `--format` mean two very different things on one command. A separate command keeps both commands simple. If maintainers prefer the `licenses` route, the builders can move over with little change.
- *A separate `src/Composer/Sbom/` namespace with dumper classes.* I started with this design. With only two formats and roughly 400 lines total, I kept everything in the command so the change is easier to review. If more formats are added, or the builders need to be reused elsewhere (for example by `audit`), extracting them is a mechanical refactor.
- *An `--output=<file>` option.* I left it out. Output goes to stdout like `licenses --format=json`, and shell redirection covers the use case. It can be added later without breaking anything.
- *Deterministic output (no timestamp, UUID derived from the lock hash).* I did not do this because both specs expect a creation time and a unique serial or namespace for each document. Component order and content are deterministic for a given lock file, so diffing two SBOMs only shows the metadata as different.
- *Format names like `cyclonedx-json`/`spdx-json`.* Both formats are JSON only for now, so I used the shorter names. A future XML or tag-value variant can be added as a new value without renaming the existing ones.

## Tests

Added `tests/Composer/Test/Command/SbomCommandTest.php`. The fixture is a root package with three runtime requirements and one dev requirement. One package has full source/dist data, credentials in its dist URL and a checksum. One has two licenses. One has no license or references. The dev package has a non-SPDX license.

Run with:

```shell
if [ -x vendor/bin/pest ]; then vendor/bin/pest 'tests/Composer/Test/Command/SbomCommandTest.php'; else vendor/bin/phpunit 'tests/Composer/Test/Command/SbomCommandTest.php'; fi
```

Cases:

- `testCycloneDxIsTheDefaultFormat`: Without `--format` the output is CycloneDX 1.6 with version 1, a valid `urn:uuid` v4 serial number, a UTC timestamp and Composer as the tool component.
- `testCycloneDxSerialNumberIsUniquePerRun`: Two runs produce different serial numbers.
- `testCycloneDxRootComponent`: The exact shape of `metadata.component` for the root package.
- `testCycloneDxComponentsAreSortedAndScoped`: Components are sorted, are `library` type and use the purl as `bom-ref`. The dev package is `optional` and the others are `required`.
- `testCycloneDxComponentDetails`: Group/name split, a single SPDX license id, `(MIT OR Apache-2.0)` expression, a non-SPDX license written as `name`, vcs and distribution references with reference comments and SHA-1 hash, and keys left out when there is no data.
- `testCycloneDxDoesNotLeakCredentials`: The dist URL password does not appear anywhere in the output.
- `testCycloneDxDependencies`: Root and per-package `dependsOn` edges. Platform requirements (`php`, `ext-json`) are left out.
- `testCycloneDxNoDev`: `--no-dev` removes the dev component and its edge from the root.
- `testCycloneDxLocked`: `--locked` works with `installed.json` deleted and still assigns scopes from the lock file.
- `testCycloneDxLockedNoDev`: `--locked --no-dev` together.
- `testLockedWithoutLockFile`: `--locked` without a lock file throws the same error message as other commands.
- `testFormatUnknown`: An unsupported format is rejected with a clear message.
- `testSpdxDocument`: SPDX document-level fields, the namespace format and the creator.
- `testSpdxPackages`: Full package shape, dist URL vs VCS `downloadLocation` vs `NOASSERTION`, checksums, license expressions, and `NOASSERTION` for missing or non-SPDX licenses.
- `testSpdxRelationships`: The exact relationship list, including `DESCRIBES`, `DEPENDS_ON` and `DEV_DEPENDENCY_OF`.
- `testSpdxNoDev`: `--no-dev` removes the dev package and every `DEV_DEPENDENCY_OF` relationship.
- `testSpdxIdsAreUniqueWhenNamesCollide`: `foo/bar-baz` and `foo/bar_baz` get distinct SPDX IDs.
- `testAliasPackagesAreSkipped`: A branch-aliased package appears once, under its real version, and the root requirement on the alias resolves to it.
- `testProvidedNamesResolveToTheProvidingPackage`: A requirement on a virtual package resolves to the package that provides it.
- `testPurlEncodesSpecialCharactersInVersion`: `+` is percent-encoded in the purl while `version` keeps the raw value.

These tests check the output structure field by field. They do not validate it against the official CycloneDX 1.6 or SPDX 2.3 JSON schemas. Adding schema validation in CI would be a good follow-up. I left it out here to avoid adding a schema file or a new dev dependency without maintainer input.

## Compatibility & risk

- **Backwards compatibility:** Purely additive. This adds a new command and does not change any existing command, option or output. The only risk is a name clash with a plugin that already registers an `sbom` command. As with any built-in command, the built-in would win, so plugin authors in this space should be aware of it.
- **Performance:** One pass over the installed or locked packages plus link resolution through a hash map, so linear in packages × requirements. No network access. `SpdxLicenses` is created lazily, once per run.
- **Migration:** None needed. Users of SBOM plugins can switch whenever they like.
- **Things I would like reviewers to look at closely:**
  - **Output to stdout via `IO::write()`.** Anything else written to stdout, such as plugin output during the `COMMAND` event, would end up in the JSON. `licenses --format=json` has the same behavior. If you would prefer to route diagnostics to stderr or add `--output`, I can do that here.
  - **Purl version uses `getPrettyVersion()`.** Dev branches therefore appear as `dev-main` and similar. The commit is available in the references, not in the purl. I think this is the most useful choice, but I am open to adding the source reference as a purl qualifier.
  - **Licenses.** Multiple licenses are joined with `OR`, which matches Composer's documented meaning of the `license` array. Strings that are not valid SPDX are never sent as SPDX ids or expressions. They become a CycloneDX `name`, or `NOASSERTION` in SPDX.
  - **Credentials.** Credential sanitization relies on `Url::sanitize()`. Any URL format it does not catch would be written into the SBOM.
  - **Root package without a name or version.** It falls back to Composer's defaults (`__root__`, and whatever version the root package loader assigns). The output is still valid, but less informative.

## Checklist

There were no checkboxes in the template, so here is the status:
- Documentation: `doc/03-cli.md` updated.
- Tests: added; I have not included a test run result here.
- Schema validation in CI: not included; proposed as a follow-up.

items.title: Add a JSON report of lock file changes to `composer update`
items.body:
---
<!-- Please remember to select the appropriate branch:

For bug fixes pick the oldest branch where the fix applies (e.g. `2.4` if that version is affected, `1.10` if it is a critical fix that should be fixed in Composer 1, otherwise `main`)

For new features and everything else, use the main branch. -->

---

## Summary

This PR adds a `--format` option (`text` by default, or `json`) to `composer update`. With `--format=json`, the lock file operations that the solver computed are written to stdout as one JSON document. Each operation lists the package name, the operation type, whether the package is a direct dependency, and the from/to version and reference. All the usual human-readable output stays on stderr. Used with `--dry-run`, this gives tools a structured preview of what an update would change, without touching the lock file or vendor directory.

## Motivation

Right now the only way to learn what `composer update` will change is to read its text output. `--dry-run` is described as "Outputs the operations but will not execute anything", and those operations are lines like `  - Upgrading acme/foo (1.0.0 => 1.2.0)` sent to stderr. CI bots, Renovate-style update tools and PR-description generators all have to scrape those lines. That breaks easily: the wording, verbosity and colour handling are not a contract, and the text has no reference/commit information or direct-vs-transitive distinction.

Many other Composer commands already offer machine-readable output: `show`, `outdated`, `audit`, `fund`, `licenses`, `search` and `check-platform-reqs` all take `--format=json`. `update` is the command that actually changes dependencies, and it has no such option.

The data is already there. `Installer::getLockTransaction()` exposes the solved `LockTransaction`, and `UpdateCommand` already reads it to drive `--bump-after-update`. It just isn't surfaced to users in a structured form. The `TODO make this a bit prettier instead of the two text indexes?` in `LockTransaction.php` is another sign that the lock-diff data has only been treated as text so far.

This affects anyone automating dependency updates. It also gives a structured base for later work on top of update results, such as an `audit fix` style flow (#12989), so that work doesn't have to parse text output.

## What changed

- **`src/Composer/Command/UpdateCommand.php`**
  - New `--format` / `-f` option. It accepts `text` (default) or `json` and uses the same definition and suggested values as the other commands that have `--format`.
  - The format is validated early, before the Composer instance is created. Unknown values fail with `Unsupported format "<value>". See help for supported formats.` and exit code 1.
  - After `$install->run()`, if the format is `json` and the installer produced a lock transaction, the command writes `{"operations": [...]}` to stdout with `JsonFile::encode`.
  - New private `getOperationsReport()` turns `LockTransaction::getOperations()` into a list of plain arrays:
    - `install`: `name`, `type`, `direct`, `to`
    - `update`: `name`, `type`, `direct`, `from`, `to`
    - `uninstall`: `name`, `type`, `direct`, `from`
    - `from`/`to` are `{version, reference}`. `version` is the pretty version. `reference` is the source reference, falling back to the dist reference, or `null`.
    - `direct` is true when the package is in the root package's `require` or `require-dev`.
    - Mirror/metadata-only updates during `update --lock` (same name and same version) are skipped. This matches how `Installer` leaves them out of the "Lock file operations" summary and the per-package lines.
- **`doc/03-cli.md`**: documents `--format (-f)` for `update`, what the JSON contains, the stdout/stderr split, and using it with `--dry-run`.
- **`tests/Composer/Test/Command/UpdateCommandTest.php`**: new test cases, described below.

## How it works

The report is built from the same `LockTransaction` that `Installer` uses for its own "Lock file operations" output. So the JSON and the text describe the same set of changes, and nothing is re-resolved. The JSON is emitted only when a lock transaction exists. If the solver fails, `getLockTransaction()` returns `null` and stdout stays empty, so a consumer can rely on "empty stdout plus non-zero exit code" meaning resolution failed.

The stdout/stderr split follows the convention Composer already uses. Normal progress output goes through `writeError()`, and the JSON document is the only thing written to stdout via `write()`. Callers can run `composer update --dry-run --format=json 2>/dev/null | jq ...` without filtering anything.

Design decisions:

- **Report lock operations, not install operations.** The lock transaction is the meaningful diff for automation ("what changes in composer.lock"). It is also the only diff available with `--no-install` or `--dry-run`. Vendor-directory operations depend on local state and are less useful to report.
- **Mirror-only updates are skipped**, not reported as `update` with identical versions. This matches the existing text output, so the two formats never disagree about the update count.
- **Single reference field.** Most consumers want "the commit or dist hash this version points to", so I prefer the source reference and fall back to the dist reference instead of exposing both.
- **`direct` only checks the root's `require` and `require-dev`.** That is the cheap, unambiguous definition. Working out *why* a transitive package moved would need dependency-graph analysis, which I left out of this PR on purpose.

Alternatives I considered and did not pick for this PR:

- **A separate `OperationReport` class in `src/Composer/Installer/` with richer records** (a `kind` that separates `metadata-only` from real version changes, a `reasons[]` list for security blocks/cooldowns, and compare URLs for GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket). This is where I'd like the format to go, and it would help with the same-version "upgrade" confusion in #12944. But each of those fields needs its own design decisions and its own tests. Keeping this PR small means reviewers can agree on the base shape and the output channel first. The JSON is an object with an `operations` key so new per-operation or top-level fields can be added later without breaking consumers.
- **Adding `--format` to `require` and `remove` at the same time.** Both run an update internally and would benefit. Their output flow is a bit different, though (for example, `require` rolls back `composer.json` on failure), so I'd rather do them in a follow-up once the format here is agreed.
- **Writing JSON to a file (`--output=report.json`).** Stdout plus `--format` is how every other Composer command does machine-readable output, so I stayed consistent.

## Tests

Added to `tests/Composer/Test/Command/UpdateCommandTest.php`:

- `testJsonFormatReportsInstallsOnStdout`: fresh update with one direct and one transitive dependency. Checks the full JSON document on stdout (`direct` true/false, `to` version/reference), checks that the normal "Lock file operations" and "Locking ..." lines are still on stderr, and checks that no JSON leaks into stderr.
- `testJsonFormatReportsUpdatesAndUninstalls`: with an existing lock file, checks that an upgraded package is reported as `update` with `from`/`to`, and a package no longer required as `uninstall` with `from`. Also checks that the text output still shows "Upgrading" and "Removing".
- `testJsonFormatTreatsDevRequiresAsDirect`: a package only in `require-dev` is reported with `direct: true`.
- `testJsonFormatPrefersSourceReferenceAndFallsBackToDistReference`: a package with both source and dist reports the source reference. A dist-only package reports the dist reference.
- `testJsonFormatSkipsMirrorOnlyUpdates`: `update --lock` where only the dist URL/reference changed produces `{"operations": []}`.
- `testJsonFormatOutputsNothingOnStdoutWhenResolutionFails`: an unsatisfiable requirement gives a non-zero exit code, empty stdout, and the usual "Your requirements could not be resolved" message on stderr.
- `testTextFormatDoesNotWriteJsonToStdout`: explicit `--format=text` keeps stdout empty and the existing output unchanged.
- `testUnsupportedFormatFails`: `--format=xml` exits with 1 and prints the unsupported-format message.

To run them:

```
vendor/bin/phpunit tests/Composer/Test/Command/UpdateCommandTest.php
vendor/bin/phpunit --filter JsonFormat tests/Composer/Test/Command/UpdateCommandTest.php
```

## Compatibility & risk

- **Backwards compatibility:** the option defaults to `text`, and nothing changes in text mode: same output, same streams, same exit codes. `-f` was not used as a shortcut by `update` before, so there is no clash.
- **Performance:** one extra pass over the already-computed lock operations, and only when `--format=json` is given. No extra solving or network access.
- **Without `--dry-run`:** `--format=json` still works and reports the lock changes that were actually written. The docs describe `--dry-run` as the main use case but don't require it.
- **Things I'd like reviewers to look at closely:**
  - The JSON is written whenever a lock transaction exists, even if `run()` later returns non-zero (for example, a failure in `extractDevPackages` or during the install step). I think reporting what was computed is the right behaviour, with the exit code as the success signal, but I'm open to restricting it to `$result === 0`.
  - The JSON goes through `$io->write()` at normal verbosity, so `-q`/`--quiet` currently suppresses it as well. If the report should survive `--quiet`, it needs to be written at `IOInterface::QUIET` verbosity. I'd like a maintainer's view on the expected behaviour.
  - `direct` is computed from the root package's requires as loaded in `UpdateCommand`. With `--with` temporary constraints, the set of direct dependencies doesn't change, but it's worth confirming that matches expectations.
  - The output schema (`operations[].name/type/direct/from/to`) becomes a contract once released. Please check the field names before this ships.
- **Migration:** none needed. Tools that scrape the text output keep working and can switch to `--format=json` when they're ready.

items.title: composer very slow on 2.9.6 and 2.9.7; fast on 2.9.5
items.body:
Hi,

My environment is composer on PHP 8.4 on Docker for Mac. Beginning v2.9.6 and continuing on v2.9.7, composer has become extremely slow. It's fast on 2.9.5.

It slows down based on the presence of one or more `scripts` in combination with the presence of `autoload.classmap`. Each script registered progressively slows it by around 2 seconds per script.  `--no-scripts --no-plugins` does not avoid the slowdown. 

The timing is directly related to the *size of the directory defined in classmap* x *number of scripts registered*.

## composer.json

Here's a minimal composer.json to reproduce it:

```json
{
  "name": "test/test",
  "autoload": {
    "classmap": [
      "modules"
    ]
  },
  "scripts": {
    "test01": "echo Hi",
    "test02": "echo Hi",
    "test03": "echo Hi",
    "test04": "echo Hi",
    "test07": "echo Hi",
    "test09": "echo Hi",
    "test10": "echo Hi",
    "test11": "echo Hi",
    "test12": "echo Hi",
    "test13": "echo Hi",
    "test14": "echo Hi",
    "test15": "echo Hi",
    "test16": "echo Hi",
    "test17": "echo Hi",
    "test18": "echo Hi",
    "test19": "echo Hi",
    "test20": "echo Hi"
  }
}

``` 

It's in a project where I have a decent number of php files in `modules`.

- If you remove the entry under `autoload.classmap`, it is fast
- Timing is worse for larger `classmap` directories, better for smaller ones.
- It gets progressively slower the more scripts you add at the rate of number of scripts x size of classmap directory.
- This example takes about 30 seconds to run "composer" in the CLI, just to show usage.

## Timing variation based on version

On 2.9.6, 28 seconds

In summary:

- Composer is slow on 2.9.6+ based on the presence of both `scripts` and `autoload.classmap` pointing to a large project.
- It's progressively slower the more scripts it has

My theory: it looks to me as if something is re-scanning the classmap filesystem for each script registered, leading to a progressively larger timing.

## Workaround

Locking composer to 2.9.5 works around this problem for my team, however I note there are two CVEs with that release so it's not a long term solution.

## Finally...

Thank you composer team, your ongoing efforts with this project are amazing and are greatly appreciated by all PHP developers worldwide. Amazing stuff.

items.title: Composer update: filter packages with security advisories from pool
items.body:
Please note, this is still a very rough draft missing tests, cleanup and taking a few shortcuts. However, feedback is already appreciated.

### Idea

Composer already has an audit functionality that reports any package used by a project with security advisories as part of an install/update/audit command. This PR takes this one step further and filters any packages with security advisories from the pool of available packages during a `composer update`command before the pool get optimized.

The functionality uses cached metadata files wherever possible. However, it is possible that it will trigger a call to the security advisories API endpoint on packagist.org if multiple Composer repositories are defined and not all packages were  looked up before on packagist.org.

This could potentially replace the need for projects to install a special package defining conflicts with packages that have security advisories.

### Sample composer.json
```
{
    "name": "acme/project",
    "version": "1.0",
    "repositories": [
```

feat: allow installation of packages only from trusted vendors
items.body:
This patch adds a new feature to allow the installation of packages only from trusted vendors.
If a required package (whether it is a direct or a transient dependency) is not in the "trusted" allow list, the installation will fail.

This option is especially useful to prevent [supply chain attacks](https://dunglas.dev/2018/11/about-the-dependencies-of-symfony/).
It allows detecting when dependencies coming from new, untrusted vendors are installed, for instance, when
a dependency of the root package adds a new transient dependency.

All packages from a specific vendor can be allowed by using the `vendor/*` special syntax.

Example:

```json
{
    "trusted": [
        "api-platform/*",
        "symfony/*",
        "doctrine/*",
        "psr/*",
        "dunglas/doctrine-json-odm"
    ]
}
```

With the previous configuration, Composer will only allow installation of packages provided by the `api-platform`, `symfony`,
`doctrine` and `psr` vendors as well as `dunglas/doctrine-json-odm` (but not other packages from `dunglas`).

We plan to use this new feature in Symfony and API Platform to ensure that our CI fails when a new, unaudited, package pops up because one of our dependencies now requires it.

This is also useful for all other security-sensitive projects when you want to be sure of what is installed and executed.

I first discussed this feature with @Seldaek and @nicolas-grekas during SymfonyCon 2022, and I'll present this feature in-depth on Friday during AFUPday 2023.
